doc: Declarative policy for scripts/check-r75.js (R75 / R100.A2). Banned literals live here as data, never assembled in executable source, so the checker cannot evade its own scan. .json is not in scan.includeExtensions, so this file is not self-matched.
patternNote: The three swallowed-error forms are DISTINCT token classes on purpose. A single aggregated empty-catch class would let a deleted null-returning catch pay for an introduced undefined-returning one — the same substitution loophole R75 exists to close. Each pattern normalizes formatting only: optional async, empty or named or typed or parenthesised parameter, and arbitrary whitespace.

suppressions.note: R75 permits this directive when the same line carries a non-empty reason. Non-empty is the whole rule: no minimum length, no ASCII or alphanumeric requirement, no issue number. The exception applies to this directive occurrence only; other banned tokens on the same line still count.

scopeNote: Application AND test sources are in scope, top-level and nested, including co-located *.spec.* / *.test.* files; R131 records that reading R75 as src-only was a misreading. Fixture DATA is out of scope only because .json is not an executable extension.
